title: SLO-driven session slicing and cost localization playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

Purpose: Provide an operator- and product-friendly playbook for slicing long LLM sessions (chat or multi-turn inference) into runtime-aligned chunks that preserve user-perceived quality while minimizing cross-tenant cost leakage. This doc ties SLOs to concrete slicing heuristics, telemetry dashboards, alert thresholds, and an incident runbook for mis-slicing-induced regressions.

Scope
- Applies to: Redwood hosted API and Dedicated routing layers that perform server-side batching, KV/prefix caching, and warmset affinity.
- Excludes: client-side truncation policies (client SDKs own that) and model-training pipelines.

Definitions
- Session slice: a contiguous sequence of tokens within a user session that is treated as a single inference request by the serving runtime (including batching and KV cache semantics).
- Cost localization: the process of ensuring token/compute costs are attributed and limited to the session/tenant that generated them (queued prefetches, cache warming, and auxiliary reranks included).
- Quality SLO: percent of requests where first-token latency < 150ms and final-response perplexity delta vs baseline model < 5% on canonical prompt set.

Why slicing matters
- Large sessions produce hot KV traces that force long-lived warmsets and biased batch shapes -> increased tail latency and per-token cost.
- Naive slicing (fixed token windows) can break coherence for system prompts, tool calling contexts, and tool state.
- Good slicing reduces redundant compute, improves batch packing, and makes cost attribution tractable across multi-tenant pools.

High-level design principles
1) SLO-first: choose slice boundaries so that the 95th/99th tail of latency stays within SLO while keeping quality regression < step budget.
2) Semantic-aware boundaries: prefer semantic cut points (turn boundaries, tool-call boundaries) over fixed token counts.
3) Conservative cache semantics: maintain a compact prefix copy for short-range coherence and a looser long-term reference for conversational context.
4) Localize prefetches and warmups with tenant credits to avoid cross-tenant cost bleeding.

Heuristics and operator knobs (recommended defaults)
- Default max-slice-tokens: 1024 for chat sessions with existing context < 3k tokens; reduce to 512 for cross-tenant-mixed pools.
- Soft boundary detection: apply sentence/turn break heuristic (stop-token + punctuation) with minimum lookback 32 tokens.
- Tool-call pinning: when a tool call is present in the last 128 tokens, extend slice to include tool output framing to preserve continuity.
- KV cache lifespan: short-lived slices -> kv-prefix-ttl = 15s; for heavyweight sessions with streaming > set to 120s + operator approval.
- Prefetch budget per-tenant: 5 warmset prefetches / minute by default; can be increased for Dedicated customers under committed capacity.

Telemetry and dashboards (recommended metrics)
- Slice metrics (per-slice): slice_tokens, slice_duration_ms, batch_size_at_slice, kv_hits_at_slice, prefetch_count, tenant_credit_used.
- Quality signals (per-session): user_prompt_loss_delta, next_token_accuracy_sample, tool-call-success-rate.
- Cost signals: tokens_charged_per_slice, gpu_ms_per_slice, prefetch_gpu_ms.
- SLOs and thresholds (dashboard rows):

Table: recommended alert thresholds
| metric | scope | warning | critical | rationale |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| first_token_latency_p95 | global | 120ms | 150ms | Catch tail growth early |
| slice_kv_hit_rate | tenant | 65% | 45% | Low hit rate -> wasted compute |
| prefetch_gpu_ms/tenant_min | tenant | 300ms/min | 800ms/min | Indicates cost leakage |
| session_quality_regression | cohort | 2% | 5% | Protect user experience |

Dashboard layout guidance
- Cluster-level overview: SLO burn rate, aggregate slice tokens, median batch size, cross-tenant prefetch heatmap.
- Tenant drilldown: per-tenant slice histogram, recent regression examples with prompts, tenant credit balance.
- Investigation panes: trace links to span-level batch composition, KV-shard map, and kernel switch events.

Runbook: investigating a slicing-induced regression (step-by-step)
1) Triage the alert: identify which signal tripped (latency vs quality vs cost).
2) Capture a reproducible session: use synthetic-replay harness to re-run the last 15 slices with the exact model variant and routing policy. CLI: rw-replay --session-id <id> --model <variant> --limit 15
3) Inspect traces: open the batch composition view; look for high variance in batch_size_at_slice or frequent kernel-switch spans.
4) KV analysis: check kv_reads vs kv_misses for that tenant; if kv_misses > 40% investigate prefix TTL and shard locality.
5) If user-quality is degraded: compare user_prompt_loss_delta across slices. If > 3%, mark rollback flag and open model-variant fallback.
6) Mitigation options (ordered):
   a) Fast rollback of slice-policy: set default max-slice-tokens -> 256 for the tenant (operator CLI).
   b) Temporarily disable prefetch for tenant: tenant-config set --no-prefetch <tenant-id>.
   c) Increase kv-prefix-ttl for session affinity windows in the region while adding guard rails to tenant credits.
7) Post-mitigation monitoring: monitor the SLO burn and run synthetic replay for 30 minutes.
8) Postmortem: assign action items and update the slice heuristic parameters if a regression is confirmed.

Operator CLI examples
- Toggle conservative slicing for a tenant:
  rw-tenant-config update <tenant-id> --max-slice-tokens 256 --kv-prefix-ttl 60
- Pause prefetching for a region:
  rw-runtime set-prefetch --region eu-west-1 --enabled false --reason "investigating slice regression"
- Run a session replay (developer sandbox):
  rw-replay --session-id s_92b3 --model rdx-v1.3-quant --trace > replay.log

Evaluation and regression guardrails
- Every change to slice heuristics must go through: unit tests (synthetic workload), canary (1% traffic for 24h), and an automated regression-check job against the canonical prompt set.
- Regression signal gating: do not roll a slicing parameter change to >10% traffic unless session_quality_regression < 1% over canary window and first_token_latency_p95 improvement > 10ms.

Post-incident retrospective checklist
- What happened: timeline of slice-policy changes, rollout windows, and affected tenants.
- Why: root cause (heuristic drift, model change, unexpected long-turn patterns).
- Detection: which dashboard/alert first surfaced issue and time-to-detect.
- Mitigation effectiveness: which operator action (CLI rollback, prefetch pause) produced most improvement and time-to-stabilize.
- Action items: code owner, ETA, priority, verification steps.

Roadmap items (next 12 months)
- Q1: launch semantic-turn-boundary detector (ML small model within gateway) to reduce unnecessary slice extensions.
- Q2: tenant-prefetch-crediting feature + UI in Console for Dedicated customers.
- Q3: integrate slice-cost-attribution into billing pipeline for per-slice tagging.
- Q4: automated slice-safety guard implemented in runtime to prevent slice heuristics from producing > 2x cost variance vs baseline.
